# Monaco pins and bundles DOMPurify below the patched versions

## Context

The operator reported four DOMPurify Dependabot alerts after the overnight dependency update. Live default branch `dev` at `ea54d5ff89eef87cdb3ade0a2f0e17fdf79ca7bf` contains:

- `mermaid@11.17.2 → dompurify ^3.3.3 → 3.4.13` (already above the four advisory floors).
- `monaco-editor@0.56.0 → dompurify 3.4.8` (exact pin; vulnerable nested lock entry).

The four open alerts all name `package-lock.json`, transitive development dependency `dompurify`:

| Alert | Advisory | First patched version |
|---|---|---|
| [222](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/security/dependabot/222) | [GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7) | 3.4.13 |
| [186](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/security/dependabot/186) | [GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4) | 3.4.12 |
| [164](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/security/dependabot/164) | [GHSA-cmwh-pvxp-8882](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-cmwh-pvxp-8882) | 3.4.11 |
| [155](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/security/dependabot/155) | [GHSA-vxr8-fq34-vvx9](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/security/advisories/GHSA-vxr8-fq34-vvx9) | 3.4.9 |

The alerts were created earlier and updated at 2026-09-05T00:49:36Z. This is the current affected dependency graph, not a claim that four advisories were newly published overnight.

## The Problem

A dependency override can replace the installed nested npm package but cannot replace the sanitizer Monaco actually executes. The published Monaco distribution embeds its own DOMPurify copy.

Measured directly from the official `monaco-editor-0.56.0.tgz`:

- `esm/vs/base/browser/dompurify/dompurify.js` carries DOMPurify **3.4.8**.
- `esm/vs/base/browser/domSanitize.js` imports that relative vendor module, not the npm `dompurify` package.
- The distributed `dev/vs/editor-ECyZhXSU.js` and `min/vs/editor-KLE6jdfb.js` chunks also contain version **3.4.8**.
- Neo's `src/main/addon/MonacoEditor.mjs#loadFiles` loads `node_modules/monaco-editor/min/vs` directly.

Consequently, an npm-only override could make dependency scanners green while leaving the browser sanitizer unchanged.

This verifies affected-version presence, not a demonstrated XSS exploit in Neo. These advisories require specific hooks/configuration; no exploitability claim or blanket exemption is made here.

## The Architectural Reality

DOMPurify is indirect but not absent from the editor: Monaco uses it for internal HTML/Markdown sanitization. The runtime source comes through VS Code's vendor copy. Upstream already [reverted a dependency-only bump](https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/pull/5347) for this reason, and [Monaco issue 5454](https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/issues/5454) tracks the bundled-copy problem.

Registry verification on 2026-09-05: Monaco latest is **0.56.0**, still pinned to **3.4.8**. DOMPurify latest is **3.4.14**; **3.4.13** meets all four listed advisory floors.

Existing root `overrides` in `package.json` addresses gray-matter/js-yaml, but that precedent does not alter already bundled JavaScript. No Engine API or ADR change is needed for a corrected upstream package.

## The Fix

**Current disposition: no corrected upstream distribution; a reproducible consumer-build candidate is now validated below.** Keep the alerts visible until the selected production integration repairs both metadata and executed assets.

Upgrade the pinned Monaco package when its shipped editor assets and dependency metadata both contain patched DOMPurify, then regenerate the lockfile and verify the actual editor asset path.

If an earlier local remediation is required, it must be a reproducible Monaco build using patched DOMPurify at module resolution and a verified Neo loader/worker integration. That is a build integration choice, not a package-only override. Do not introduce minified-bundle surgery or an install-time patch as an implicit workaround.

Revalidation trigger: an upstream release/update on microsoft/monaco-editor#5454 or an explicitly selected local rebuild approach.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A clean install resolves every DOMPurify lock entry above all four affected ranges; dependency output identifies the complete parent chains.
- [ ] AC-2: Monaco's browser-loaded sanitizer is verified patched from the actual distributed/generated assets. A lockfile-only update does not satisfy this.
- [ ] AC-3: Neo's Monaco editor boots, edits, and starts its language worker, with a sanitized HTML/Markdown rendering smoke and no new load failures.
- [ ] AC-4: Post-merge: GitHub reevaluates alerts 155, 164, 186 and 222 as fixed by the dependency update; do not dismiss them to simulate remediation.

## Out of Scope

Mermaid updates (its current sanitizer is already patched for these four alerts), replacing Monaco with another editor, unrelated dependency upgrades, and claiming exploitability from version matching alone.

## Avoided Traps

- An override that replaces an unused npm copy while the browser keeps executing the embedded old copy.
- Downgrading Monaco to remove dependency metadata without checking its embedded sanitizer.
- Assuming a dependency labeled development cannot reach the browser.
- Editing third-party minified files manually.

## Extended investigation — 2026-09-05

The published `latest` remains Monaco **0.56.0**; `next` is **0.56.0-dev-20260625**, whose metadata also pins DOMPurify **3.4.8**. All four alerts remain open. Mermaid's installed **3.4.13** satisfies these four advisory floors.

### Exposure in the inspected integration

The four advisories require, respectively: a prior custom Trusted Types policy on the reused instance; persistent `setConfig()` plus an allowlist-mutating attribute hook; custom-element handling plus an `afterSanitizeElements` policy; or `IN_PLACE` plus an element-removal hook. The shipped Monaco `domSanitize.js` builds per-call configuration, accepts string input, and does not configure those combinations. Its attribute predicate uses per-element `keepAttr`.

Executed the current Neo wrapper's AMD editor and JavaScript worker: diagnostics were empty; a custom HTML-capable Markdown hover removed event handlers and `javascript:` links, with no marker execution or page error. Separately instrumented the official ESM sanitizer: three exercised calls all used string input, no `IN_PLACE`, no custom-element configuration, no custom Trusted Types policy, and zero `setConfig`/`clearConfig` calls. This bounds the observed path; it does not certify every embedder or replace the dependency remediation.

### Reproducible consumer-build candidate

A working alternative now exists. Using Monaco's [official esbuild smoke-build pattern](https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/blob/main/test/smoke/package-esbuild.ts), compiled the published **0.56.0 ESM modules** while resolving the vendor import in `domSanitize.js` to the official **DOMPurify 3.4.14** ESM distribution. This substitutes a module at build time; no third-party source or minified bundle was edited.

- The esbuild metadata proves the actual `domSanitize.js → purify.es.mjs` edge, with the old vendor module absent.
- Generated editor JavaScript, CSS, font and all five standard worker entry points.
- Browser candidate reports **3.4.14**, boots the editor, reads its live model through the TypeScript worker, and passes the sanitized-hover smoke with zero page errors or failed asset responses.
- Two builds with esbuild **0.28.2** produce the same editor bundle: **4,483,078 bytes**, SHA-256 `d02e1a8915eeb1bb4a6d7dd0961e4f4855cbb583d3c9534cc4ad700153c57410`.

This is an isolated candidate, not the shipped Neo runtime. Production adoption still needs a maintained asset-build entry, Neo loader/worker URL integration, a patched dependency/lock graph, and the existing real-wrapper lifecycle tests against those generated assets. The candidate carries a diagnostic version export that would not be part of the production API. No repository files or alert dispositions changed during these probes.

The complete remediation can therefore proceed through a consumer build if upstream publication remains delayed; the current installed package continues to need repair.

## Rebuild approach selected, 2026-09-15

Upstream is unchanged: `monaco-editor` 0.56.0 is still latest and still pins DOMPurify 3.4.8. #5454 is open. The operator's goal is zero Dependabot alerts, which selects the "explicitly selected local rebuild approach" named in this ticket's revalidation trigger. Taking it.

**Spike, run against this repo's installed `monaco-editor` 0.56.0 with esbuild 0.28.2, already a dependency.** Monaco's ESM `vs/base/browser/domSanitize.js` imports its DOMPurify as a separate module, `./dompurify/dompurify.js`, so one resolve rule at build time swaps it for `dompurify`'s exported ESM entry. Nothing is edited in any minified file.

| output | size | DOMPurify inside |
|---|---|---|
| `editor.js` (IIFE, exposes `monaco`) | 4,483,251 B | 3.4.13 only |
| `editor.css` + codicon font | 157 KB + 141 KB | — |
| five workers (editor, css, html, json, typescript) | 0.3–7.0 MB each | none |

The vendored `dompurify.js` module is in no output graph.

**Shape**, following the existing vendor-bundle precedent (`parse5`, `marked`, `mermaid`, `highlight`):
- `buildScripts/build/monaco.mjs` writes to `dist/monaco/`.
- `bundle-browser-deps` runs it, so CI builds it where it builds the others.
- `.npmignore` re-includes it for publishing.
- `MonacoEditor` loads the bundle and supplies `MonacoEnvironment` for the workers.
- An `overrides` entry removes the nested 3.4.8 lock entry.
- The component spec's AMD-specific arms become bundle arms, plus a sanitizer-version assertion.

**Cost to weigh at merge:** the published package grows by roughly 14 MB, the TypeScript worker alone 7 MB. In exchange, a consumer no longer installs `monaco-editor` for the addon.
